questions.html: Slotted aloha is a variant of the Aloha media-access protocol that divides time into equal-sized $\text{“slots"}$ and only starts transmissions at the beginning of a slot time. In a slotted aloha system, suppose there are $5$ nodes that each transmit with probability of $p$. What is the probability, in a given slot time, that one of the nodes successfully transmits a packet?

questions.html:
Suppose a router has built up the routing table shown below. The router can deliver packets directly over interfaces $0$ and $1,$ or it can forward packets to routers $\mathrm{R} 2, \mathrm{R} 3$, or $\mathrm{R} 4$.
$$
\begin{array}{l|l|l}
\hline \text{SubnetNumber} & \text{SubnetMask} & \text{NextHop} \\
\hline 128.96 .39 .0 & 255.255 .255 .128 & \text{Interface 0} \\
128.96 .39 .128 & 255.255 .255 .128 & \text{Interface 1} \\
128.96 .40 .0 & 255.255 .255 .128 & \text{R2} \\
192.4 .153 .0 & 255.255 .255 .192 & \text{R3} \\
\langle \text{default} \rangle & & \text{R4} \\
\hline
\end{array}$$
Which the following statements is/are true:

options.html: For a packet addressed to the destination $128.96.39.10,$ router uses $\text{R4}$ as the next hop.
For a packet addressed to the destination $128.96.40.12,$ router uses $\mathrm{R} 2$ as the next hop.
For a packet addressed to the destination $192.4.153.17,$ router uses $\text{R3}$ as the next hop.
For a packet addressed to the destination $192.4.153.90,$ router uses $\mathrm{R} 4$ as the next hop.

questions.solution:
Answer: B, C, D

questions.html:
Consider a sliding–window transfer mechanism where both the sender and receiver use a window of size $3$. The retransmission timeout (RTO) is $2 \times \mathrm{RTT}$. Packets numbered $1$ through $6$ are to be sent.
Packets $3$ and $6$ are lost during their first transmission.

Each correctly received packet generates cumulative ACK.
Assume fast retransmission is implemented such that retransmission takes place either upon receipt of the first duplicate ACK or upon timeout.

Determine how many $\mathrm{RTTs}$ from the start elapse before packet $6$ is transmitted again.
questions.solution:
Answer: B

questions.html:
Let $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ be two stations attempting to transmit on an Ethernet. $\text{A's}$ frames will be numbered $\text{A1, A2},$ and so on, and $\text{B's}$ similarly.
Suppose $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ simultaneously attempt to send frame $1.$ Consider the following events.

  • $\text{A1}$ collides with $\text{B1, A}$ wins backoff race immediately after the first collision of $\text{A1}.$
  • $\text{A2}$ collides with $\text{B1, A}$ wins backoff race immediately after the first collision of $\text{A2}.$
  • $\text{A3}$ collides with $\text{B1}.$

What is the probability that $\text{A}$ wins this third backoff race immediately after the first collision of $\text{A3}?$
questions.solution:
Answer: B
